I like looking at obscure supplements. Sometimes I even order them. For the most part they're worthless, but sometimes I'll hit the jackpot and get some minor, slightly noticeable effects. Maybe it's placebo, maybe it's not, who knows. Mostly I like researching them and getting that glimmer of "this might actually work and do some good, maybe I'll even gain a few pounds of muscle on it" excitement.

This one in particular, beta ecdysterone, looked particularly promising. For those of you who haven't heard of it [almost everyone I'm guessing], beta ecdysterone, or just ecdysterone for short, is a compund found in plants and bugs, and it acts as a hormone in those bugs. A bug androgen, basically. There were some shady old Soviet studies where it compared pretty favorably to the steroid Winstrol, which isn't a very powerful muscle builder, but still, a steroid!

Modern sources seemed to also conclude, albeit more hesistantly, that it works. For example, examine.com did a writeup on it, and examine.com is known for calling almost all supplements bullshit.

At this point I'm feeling pretty excited, and thinking about ordering some. But then, after a little more research, I find that, woah, apparently both spinach and quinoa both contain ecdysterone in high enough quantities to rival the amount found in supplements with just a couple of servings. So there's no need to buy any pills after all!

I was already consuming spinach in decent quantity, but I up my intake and consistency, and in addition, I buy some quinoa for the first time. I don't particularly enjoy it, but I find that adding some in my oatmeal is quite bearable, gives it an interesting texture. The spinach is good with vinegar and crumbled cheese, it's easy to eat quite a lot of it that way.

And you know what? I think it actually did me some good. Naturally, spinach and quinoa aren't going to be bad for you, and I don't think it was much like what winstrol would have been, but it definitely had some minor effects, better than most supplements, anyways. I feel like my recovery time improved, and I definitely got sore less. I still keep some quinoa around, and toss it in my oatmeal on occasion. It's good to know something so simple can have such a profound effect.
